chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibn Fuddal, from al-Halabi and Zurarah, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Alone, the Needless, without an interior. Verily, the Spirit is a creation from His creations. It is a helper, aid, and a source of strength. Allah places it in the hearts of the messengers and the Believers.

key_terms.أَحَدٌ: The Alone, One of a kind

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the Spirit (Ruh) in Shia theology according to al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to articulate the Shia doctrine of the created nature of the Ruh, distinguishing it from the divine essence while affirming its role as a divine bestowal of strength (nusrat wa ta'yid) in the hearts of the faithful. This aligns with the Mu'tazili-influenced rational theology of the early Shia scholars, who emphasized that 'breathing' of the Spirit is an act of creation rather than an emanation of God's very self, thereby preserving divine transcendence (tanzih).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa said, on the authority of Ibn Fuddal, on the authority of al-Halabi and Zurarah, that Abu `Abd Allah (AS) said: “

Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is the Alone, the Needless, without an interior. Verily, the Spirit is a creation from His Creations. It is a helper, aid, and a source of strength. Allah places it is in the hearts of the messengers and the Believers.”
